claims.text: Large language models pretrained on code demonstrate strong capabilities in generating programs from natural language inputs.
L2CEval systematically evaluates language-to-code generation across 7 tasks spanning semantic parsing, math reasoning, and Python programming.
Model size, pretraining data, instruction tuning, and prompting methods affect language-to-code generation performance in LLMs.
L2CEval assesses confidence calibration of LLMs in language-to-code tasks.
Human evaluations identify typical failure modes across different language-to-code tasks and models.

evidence.description: Abstract states that LLMs pretrained on code 'have demonstrated strong capabilities in generating programs from natural language inputs.'

Abstract describes L2CEval as 'a systematic evaluation of the language-to-code generation capabilities of LLMs on 7 tasks across the domain spectrum of semantic parsing, math reasoning, and Python programming'.
Abstract states the evaluation involves 'analyzing the factors that potentially affect their performance, such as model size, pretraining data, instruction tuning, and different prompting methods.'
Abstract notes 'In addition, we assess confidence calibration'.
Abstract states 'and conduct human evaluations to identify typical failures across different tasks and models.'

methodologies.name: L2CEval
methodologies.description: A evaluation benchmark and framework assessing LLM language-to-code capabilities across 7 tasks, alongside confidence calibration and human evaluation of failures.

limitations.text: Existing studies lack a comprehensive evaluation of LLMs' language-to-code generation capabilities.
Existing studies focus narrowly on specific tasks, model architectures, or learning paradigms, leading to fragmented understanding.

future_work.text: Update evaluation results for future models (e.g., LLaMA-3, StarCoder2) on the project website.
